abstract: Flowers are highly diverse in shape, scent, and colour and may differ strikingly even among closely related species. Floral traits experience correlational selection favouring trait combinations that maximise plant reproduction, leading to outstanding questions on how floral trait divergence evolves in closely related species. In this review, we take a quantitative genetic perspective and ask whether and how the genetic architecture of floral trait divergence depends on adaptation to specific pollination systems and how it informs on the dynamics of the assembly of floral traits during divergence. After reviewing results from studies mapping divergent floral traits in closely related species, we emphasise the value of combining trait mapping approaches with approaches that identify genomic variation differentiating species boundaries. We show how the combination of these approaches has been successful in recent studies and how it could improve our understanding of floral diversification.

Les traits floraux subissent une sélection corrélée favorisant une combinaison de traits qui maximise la reproduction de la plante. Dans cette revue de la littérature, nous adoptons l'angle de la génétique quantitative pour nous demander si, et alors comment, l'architecture génétique de traits floraux divergents dépend de l'adaptation à des systèmes de pollinisation spécifiques, et comment cela informe sur la dynamique d'assemblage des traits floraux lors de leur divergence.
